items.title: How can a user uninstall a Chrome JavaScript SpeechRecognition.install language pack?
items.body:
In Chrome you can now run the JavaScript command:

SpeechRecognition.install({
          langs: ["en-US"],
          processLocally: true,
        })

Any website can run it to install a language pack to run speech recognition locally. However as explained at https://issues.chromium.org/issues/521896368 , once you install a language pack then even if processLocally = false the Web Speech API will still use the local language pack if it is installed. There is no way for the user to know if it is using the cloud or local unless they disable their Internet. If speech recognition still works with Internet disabled then it is being processed locally. That presents a problem with users that want to go back to using the cloud because of poor performance from the local language pack because there are no instructions for uninstalling the language pack. There are no settings in Chrome. The closest setting that I can find in Chrome is "Live Caption". I found that if I turn on "Live Caption" and then remove the English language pack then the Web Speech API will start using the cloud again. But it is a very temporary fix. Within a few minutes it seems that Chrome automatically goes back to using the local language pack for SpeechRecognition. The SpeechRecognition.available will show that the language pack is back to "available" instead of "downloadable" and the Web Speech API will start being processed locally again.

So how can a user uninstall a SpeechRecognition language pack? It seems like a poor design to not let users easily see which language packs have been installed using SpeechRecognition.install along with no information about removing them.

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class _TodoAppState extends State<TodoApp> {
  // Controller to read text from the TextField

  // The list that holds all our tasks

  // Always dispose controllers to prevent memory leaks

    _taskController.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  // Helper method: Adds a new task to the list

      setState(() {
        _tasks.add(Task(name: _taskController.text.trim()));
        _taskController.clear(); // Clear the TextField after adding
      });
    }
  }

  // Helper method: Removes ONLY completed tasks (used by AppBar icon)

    });
  }

    return Scaffold(
      // APPBAR: Title and Delete Completed Icon

        title: const Text('Stateful Widget Lab Exam'),

        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16.0),
        child: Column(
          children: [
            // Input Field

              controller: _taskController,
              decoration: const InputDecoration(
                border: OutlineInputBorder(),
                hintText: 'Enter task name',
              ),
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 10),
            
            // Add Task Button
            ElevatedButton(
              onPressed: _addTask,
              child: const Text('Add Task'),
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 10),
            
            // Expanded prevents the "Column Overflow" error by giving the ListView
            // the remaining vertical space to scroll.
            Expanded(
              child: ListView.builder(
                itemCount: _tasks.length,
                itemBuilder: (context, index) {
                  final task = _tasks[index];
                  
                  // Each task is a Card containing a ListTile
                  return Card(
                    elevation: 2,
                    margin: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(vertical: 4),
                    child: ListTile(
                      // Leading Icon: Checked or Unchecked
                      leading: Icon(
                        task.isCompleted ? Icons.check_circle : Icons.circle_outlined,
                        color: task.isCompleted ? Colors.green : Colors.grey,
                      ),
                      
                      // Title: Task text with strikethrough if completed

                        style: TextStyle(
                          decoration: task.isCompleted 
                              ? TextDecoration.lineThrough 
                              : TextDecoration.none,
                          color: task.isCompleted ? Colors.grey : Colors.black,
                        ),
                      ),
                      
                      // Trailing: Delete specific task
                      trailing: IconButton(
                        icon: const Icon(Icons.delete),
                        onPressed: () {
                          setState(() {
                            _tasks.removeAt(index);
                          });
                        },
                      ),
                      
                      // Tapping toggles the completion status
                      onTap: () {
                        setState(() {
                          task.isCompleted = !task.isCompleted;
                        });
                      },
                    ),

                },
              ),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
      
      // FLOATING ACTION BUTTON: Reset / Clear all tasks

        onPressed: _clearAllTasks,
        tooltip: 'Reset Application',
        child: const Icon(Icons.refresh),
      ),
    );
  }
}

items.title: Build update from Server to Client
items.body:
I’m working on a web application where the client/browser caches static build files (JS, CSS, etc.) for several minutes to improve performance and reduce unnecessary requests.

The problem occurs when a new build is deployed on the server while an existing client still has the previous build cached.

For example:

  1. Client loads Build A and caches its static assets for 5–10 minutes.

  2. A new version is deployed on the server, generating Build B.

  3. The client is still using the cached Build A files.

  4. The user may continue running the old version until the cache expires or they manually refresh/clear the cache.

I’d like to know whether there is a standard way to make the client automatically detect that a newer build is available and switch to the new build, without relying on a fixed cache timeout or requiring the user to manually clear their cache.

Ideally, I’m looking for something along the lines of:

Client
  ↓
Has cached Build A
  ↓
Server deploys Build B
  ↓
Client detects Build B is available
  ↓
Downloads the new assets
  ↓
Switches to Build B

I understand that frameworks such as Next.js can revalidate or regenerate content (for example, ISR), but that primarily concerns application data/content. My question is specifically about versioning and invalidating the client's cached static build assets after a new deployment.

What is the recommended production approach for this?

I’m particularly interested in how modern production applications handle this problem while still maintaining aggressive browser caching for performance.

items.title: IntersectionObserver with bxslider background-image slideshow behaves strangely
items.body:
It does lazy load the images, but when I resize the browser, the image is gone and I see the black defined for class bxslider. The observed element has the class lazy-background-loaded. But there is no image visible. I fiddled around with rootMargin and scrollMargin. But the image disappears on resize. In order to prevent the disappearance, I added another function for the resize event. The image remains on the screen, but during the resize event a flickering occurs.

Is the IntersectionObserver() suitable for a horizontal background-image slide show?

Has anyone ever successfully tried to use IntersectionObserver() in this context?

Is there a better way to tell IntersectionObserver() to permanently keep the style="background-image:url('image.jpg')" once an image has entered the viewport and not to loose it, when the windowsize changes? Is it possible to get rid of that flickering the resize function produces? (i tried a delay function, but that shows a blank screen while resizing, and when the event is completed the image shows. Not really good)

By the way: this method is not suitable for bx-slider option: infiniteLoop:true. Jumping from first to last slide shows a blank screen first and then the slide comes in.

Thanks for your answer.

//js(loaded in footer)

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
  const targets = document.querySelectorAll('.lazy-background');

  const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries, obs) => {
    entries.forEach(entry => {
      if (!entry.isIntersecting) return;
      const el = entry.target;
      const src = el.dataset.bgSrc;
      if (src) el.style.backgroundImage = `url('${src}')`;
      el.classList.replace('lazy-background', 'lazy-background-loaded');
      obs.unobserve(el);
    });
  }, {
    root: document.querySelector(".bx-viewport"),
    rootMargin: "0px",
    scrollMargin: "0px",
    threshold: 0,
  });

  targets.forEach(el => observer.observe(el));
});

//i added this resize function in order
//to prevent the images to disappear when the
//browser window is changed.
//The images remain, but a flickering occurs.

window.addEventListener('resize', function(event) {
    const targets = document.querySelectorAll('.lazy-background-loaded');
    const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries, obs) => {
    entries.forEach(entry => {
    const el  = entry.target;
    const src = el.dataset.bgSrc;
    console.log(src);
    if (src) el.style.backgroundImage = `url('${src}')`;
    el.style.backgroundImage = 'url('+src+')';
    obs.unobserve(el);
    });
 }, {root: document.querySelector(".bx-viewport"),
    rootMargin: '0px',
    scrollMargin: "0px",
    threshold: 0 
});
targets.forEach(el => observer.observe(el));
}, true);

items.title: How to force a link to open in the system browser from Telegram's in-app browser (WebView)?
items.body:
I'm building a React web application that uses TonConnect to connect TON wallets. The flow works perfectly on desktop browsers and on mobile when opened directly in Chrome.

However, when the application is opened from Telegram (via a link shared in a chat), it loads inside Telegram's built-in WebView. The wallet connection works, but after connecting, the wallet app redirects back to the page. This causes issues because the WebView doesn't handle the redirect properly – sometimes it opens a different page, and sometimes it gives an "Aw, Snap!" error.

Is there any reliable way to force a link (e.g., https://example.com) to open in the user's default system browser from Telegram's in-app browser, without requiring the user to manually copy and paste the URL?

items.title: How can I apply custom syntax highlighting colors to CodeMirror to match Prism.js Okaidia theme?
items.body:
I am building a coding tutorial website and using Prism.js (Okaidia theme) for static example boxes and CodeMirror for the interactive editor. I want to match the colors of both.

The Comparison:

  • Prism (Target): Correcty highlights CSS selectors (pink/blue), JS variables (blue), and Python built-ins (pink).

  • CodeMirror (The Issue): Even after applying custom CSS with !important, specific tokens like .selectors, variables, and built-in functions remain white or default yellow. They don't pick up the colors I defined.

What I want: How can I make CodeMirror's tokenization match Prism's style so that the user has a consistent experience across the website?"

items.title: Stripe Connect onboarding works in test mode but redirects to login in live mode
items.body:
I am developing an app which integrate Stripe as payment, but the user doesn't need the hassle going to Stripe to manage everything, they can do it in the app. So when activating Stripe on testing env it works refer to a screenshot

This is what I want, user add info and verify the identity and redirect back to my platform and then boom voila. This works on testing environment but on the next screenshots, it's different instead of landing on this screen, am getting this one

as asking me to login, my question is there anything I missed on prod? or what can I do to get onboarding screen without first login into Stripe. Because I don't want the user to interact with Stripe.

this is my code

<script>
import { loadConnectAndInitialize } from "@stripe/connect-js";
import { apiDataService } from "@/services/apiDataService";
export default {
    data() {
        return {
            stripeState: "idle",
            checkingStripeStatus: true,
            stripeData: null,
            stripeClientId: null,
            loading: false,
            error: null,
        };
    },
    methods: {
        async getStripeStatus() {
            this.checkingStripeStatus = true;
            this.error = null;
            try {
                const res = await apiDataService.stripeStatus();
                const data = res.data;
                if (data.is_fully_onboarded) {
                    this.stripeData = data;
                    this.stripeState = "connected";
                } else if (data.stripe_account_id) {
                    this.stripeData = data;
                    this.stripeClientId = data.stripe_account_id;
                    this.stripeState = "onboarding";
                    await this.$nextTick();
                    await this.initializeStripeConnect();
                } else {
                    this.stripeState = "idle";
                }
            } catch (err) {
                console.error(err);
                this.error = "Failed to fetch Stripe status";
                this.stripeState = "idle";
            } finally {
                this.checkingStripeStatus = false;
            }
        },
        async startConnect() {
            this.loading = true;
            this.error = null;
            try {
                const res = await apiDataService.connectStripe();
                const data = res.data;
                if (data.is_fully_onboarded) {
                    this.stripeData = data;
                    this.stripeState = "connected";
                    return;
                }
                if (data.needs_onboarding && data.onboarding_url) {
                    window.location.href = data.onboarding_url;
                    return;
                }
                this.stripeClientId = data.account_id;
                this.stripeState = "onboarding";
                await this.$nextTick();
                await this.initializeStripeConnect();
            } catch (err) {
                console.error(err);
                this.error = err.response?.data?.error || "Failed to create Stripe account";
            } finally {
                this.loading = false;
            }
        },
        async initializeStripeConnect() {
            if (!this.$refs.stripeContainer) {
                console.error("Stripe container not found");
                return;
            }
            const publishableKey = process.env.VUE_APP_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY;
            if (!publishableKey) {
                this.error = "Stripe publishable key not configured";
                return;
            }
            try {
                this.$refs.stripeContainer.innerHTML = "";
                const instance = await loadConnectAndInitialize({
                    publishableKey,
                    fetchClientSecret: async () => {
                        const response = await apiDataService.clientSecretEmbedding({
                            account_id: this.stripeClientId,
                        });
                        return response.data.client_secret;
                    },
                });
                const onboarding = instance.create("account-onboarding");
                this.$refs.stripeContainer.appendChild(onboarding);
                onboarding.addEventListener("onboarding_completed", () => {
                    this.stripeState = "connected";
                    this.getStripeStatus();
                });
                onboarding.addEventListener("onboarding_exited", () => {
                    this.getStripeStatus();
                });
            } catch (err) {
                console.error("Stripe error:", err);
                this.error = err.message || "Failed to initialize Stripe onboarding";
            }
        },
    },
    mounted() {
        this.getStripeStatus();
    },
};
</script>

and for template
